context.bounded_contribution: Finite-cutoff SU(2) heat-kernel Route A realization of a reflected Wilson-block Schur-Feshbach test, with geometric collar, endpoint, continuum, and gap steps isolated as open modules.

context.abstract: We give a fully specified finite-cutoff realization of a Schur--Feshbach positivity test for reflected Wilson observables. The matrix statement is the rank-one specialization of standard second-order geometry of the positive-semidefinite cone: if \[ q_\eps=\one\one^*+\eps H+\eps^2K+o(\eps^2), \] then, after eliminating the rank-one direction, the first two coefficients are \[ A=PHP, \qquad C=P\bigl(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H\bigr)P, \qquad e=n^{-1/2}\one, \quad P=I-ee^*. \] The field-theoretic contribution is an explicit same-theory block. On a finite four-dimensional reflection-symmetric lattice with gauge group $SU(2)$ and heat-kernel plaquette weight, we define three closed hairpin loops sharing a base path. A spatial-reflection odd Wilson mode $X$ and an even centered Wilson mode $Y$ generate three positive-time observables \[ F_i^\eps=1+\sqrt\eps\,b_iX+\eps c_iY, \qquad b=(1,-1,0)^T, \quad c=(0,0,1)^T. \] Their reflected Gram matrix is exactly \[ N_\eps=\one\one^T+\eps\sigma bb^T+\eps^2\tau cc^T, \qquad \sigma=\langle\Theta X,X\rangle_{\OS}\ge0, \quad \tau=\langle\Theta Y,Y\rangle_{\OS}\ge0. \] Diagonal correlation normalization is realized by rescaling the same observables, hence is an exact congruence rather than an uncontrolled entrywise quotient. The normalized block has a rank-one limit and yields \[ PHP=\sigma bb^T, \qquad C=-\sigma^2bb^T+\frac{\tau}{9}zz^T, \qquad z=(1,1,-2)^T. \] Thus the first reduced eigenvalue is $2\sigma$, while the corrected second-order null-sector eigenvalue is $2\tau/3$. The uncorrected quantity contains a spurious $\sigma^2$ term, which the Schur--Feshbach correction removes. All statements up to this point are exact at finite cutoff. Geometric collar collapse, uniform nondegeneracy along a continuum trajectory, endpoint cumulant estimates, infinite volume, and a spectral-gap implication are isolated as explicit open modules rather than claimed results.
